paragraphs: Online learning asks a model to learn as observations arrive. This paper studies binary prediction under minimal assumptions about how those observations are generated. Its central question is broader than whether one algorithm works on one familiar type of data: it asks which data processes permit learning at all for each concept class, meaning a specified family of possible prediction rules.

The authors then ask whether a single algorithm can succeed on every process that permits learning for that class. An algorithm with this property is called optimistically universal. The paper characterizes which concept classes admit such algorithms, resolves the corresponding questions about minimal data assumptions, and constructs general learning algorithms for the different cases.

The results also extend from the realizable setting, where the concept class can explain the labels, to the agnostic setting, where that match is not required. The authors establish equivalent minimal data assumptions and equivalent optimistically universal learnability across these settings. The contribution is a theoretical account of when such broad adaptability is possible.
neurips-2024-a-theory-of-optimistically-.tldr: The paper characterizes when binary online learning admits an algorithm that succeeds under every data process for which learning is possible.

paragraphs: Adversarial images are altered inputs that cause a neural network to make mistakes while looking nearly unchanged to people. AdvAD approaches this problem by treating the attack itself as a diffusion process. Its central departure is to use the mathematical structure of diffusion without relying on an additional neural network trained to generate or denoise images.

At each step, the attacked model supplies guidance that gradually moves the original image toward an adversarial example. The authors develop a theoretical foundation for this non-parametric process and report that it supports effective attacks with small overall changes. They also introduce AdvAD-X to explore the framework under an ideal scenario; that qualification matters when interpreting the enhanced version.

Experiments on an ImageNet-compatible dataset cover four neural networks spanning three architectures. AdvAD reports an average attack success rate of 99.9%, alongside an l2 distance of 1.34 and strong image-similarity measurements. The reported comparisons support the claim that, in these evaluations, attack effectiveness and visual similarity can improve together without adding a separate generative network.
neurips-2024-advad-exploring-non-paramet.tldr: AdvAD uses diffusion guided only by the attacked model to produce highly effective adversarial images with small visual changes.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning improves decision-making policies using previously collected data. Safety makes this harder, especially when the dataset covers only a limited range of behavior. WSAC addresses this problem by optimizing a policy relative to a reference policy, seeking better performance while preserving the reference policy's level of safety.

The method organizes learning as a two-player Stackelberg game. The actor, which selects actions, faces two adversarially trained value critics. These critics emphasize situations where the actor falls short of the reference policy, while keeping importance-weighted Bellman errors small. This connects policy improvement to deliberately challenging evaluations of its behavior.

The theoretical guarantees assume that the actor uses a no-regret optimization oracle. Under that condition, the authors establish safe improvement relative to any reference policy, an optimal statistical convergence rate of 1/√N, and safe improvement across a broad range of pessimism settings. A practical implementation outperforms the compared baselines across several continuous-control tasks. These experiments support the method's usefulness, while the formal claims retain their stated optimization assumption.
neurips-2024-adversarially-trained-weigh.tldr: WSAC uses adversarial critics to improve offline policies while preserving reference-policy safety, with theoretical guarantees under a no-regret optimization assumption.

paragraphs: Neural operators learn mappings between functions and offer an alternative to costly approaches for solving partial differential equations. The paper argues that these models need to capture both broad structure across a function and detailed local behavior. Existing ways of integrating information can also become computationally expensive as the number of sampled points increases.

MambaNO combines two mechanisms to address those concerns. A Mamba state space model scans the whole function to provide global integration, while an alias-free architecture handles local integration. The proposed operator has O(N) computational complexity, making its stated computational growth linear in the number of points rather than quadratic or N log N.

The authors prove a continuous-discrete equivalence property and use it to establish approximation capability for operators arising from PDEs to a desired accuracy. They also evaluate MambaNO on diverse benchmarks, including potentially multiscale solutions. The reported results achieve new leading scores with fewer parameters and better efficiency, supporting the value of combining global and local processing within this architecture.
neurips-2024-alias-free-mamba-neural-ope.tldr: MambaNO combines global Mamba processing with local alias-free integration to learn PDE operators with linear computational complexity.

paragraphs: Audio watermarks embed signals that people should not hear but that can help identify AI-generated speech. Their usefulness depends on more than being detectable immediately after insertion: they must also withstand changes to the audio. AudioMarkBench investigates this robustness as synthetic speech becomes increasingly realistic and raises concerns about impersonation and disinformation.

The benchmark examines two distinct failures. Watermark removal undermines the evidence that an audio recording was marked, while watermark forgery creates misleading evidence of a watermark. The authors assemble a Common-Voice-based dataset spanning languages, biological sexes, and ages, and evaluate three leading watermarking methods against 15 kinds of perturbations.

Testing covers no-box, black-box, and white-box settings, allowing robustness to be examined under different levels of attacker access. The findings expose vulnerabilities in the evaluated techniques and motivate both stronger protection and greater attention to fairness. The contribution is a systematic evaluation resource for comparing watermark reliability across varied speech and attack conditions, with publicly available data and code.
neurips-2024-audiomarkbench-benchmarking.tldr: AudioMarkBench evaluates audio watermark removal and forgery across diverse speech and attack settings, revealing weaknesses in current methods.

paragraphs: An agent planning under partial observability must act without knowing the full state of its environment. It must also respect what a user wants or forbids. This paper introduces parameterized belief-state query policies as a way to express such preferences and constraints in goal-oriented partially observable Markov decision processes.

The key theoretical finding concerns how a policy's expected cost changes with its parameters. Although this objective is not convex, it is piecewise constant: different parameter values can produce the same cost over regions of the search space. For finite planning horizons, this structure induces a finite discrete search space, providing a basis for optimization despite the lack of convexity.

The authors use that structure to develop algorithms with guaranteed alignment to the expressed user requirements. They prove convergence to optimal user-aligned behavior in the limit, rather than claiming that every finite run reaches the optimum. Empirical results indicate that these policies are computationally feasible, connecting the formal analysis to practical planning under uncertainty.
neurips-2024-belief-state-query-policies.tldr: Belief-state query policies make user-constrained planning under partial observability optimizable, with alignment guarantees and convergence to optimal behavior in the limit.

paragraphs: Some image segmentation requests identify an object through its relationships to other objects, rather than by naming its category alone. A description may combine where something sits with what is in front of it. DeiSAM targets these context-dependent, or deictic, prompts, where correctly following several relationships is essential to choosing the intended image region.

The system combines pretrained neural networks with differentiable logical reasoning. A large language model translates the textual description into first-order logic rules. DeiSAM then reasons forward over generated scene graphs, which represent objects and their relationships, to infer the relevant regions. It uses those conclusions to select and segment the objects.

The authors also introduce Deictic Visual Genome, a dataset pairing images with complex contextual prompts. Their experiments show substantial improvements over purely data-driven baselines on deictic promptable segmentation. The results support the usefulness of making relational reasoning an explicit part of the segmentation process, so that object selection can depend on the combined meaning of a description's relationships.
neurips-2024-deisam-segment-anything-wit.tldr: DeiSAM turns contextual image descriptions into logic rules and reasons over scene graphs to segment the intended objects more accurately.

paragraphs: A user's interests can be diverse and change over time, making them difficult to summarize with one representative point or even several separate points. This paper proposes density-based user representations to describe that variability more flexibly. The aim is to improve personalized retrieval while accounting for the fact that a system may know some interests more confidently than others.

The proposed method, GPR4DUR, uses Gaussian process regression to build these representations. The authors describe an approach that captures interest variability without manual tuning, incorporates uncertainty, and scales to large user populations. Representing uncertainty matters because recommendation involves choosing between using established knowledge and exploring less certain possibilities.

Experiments on real-world offline datasets support the method's adaptability and efficiency. Separate online experiments use simulated users and show that model uncertainty can help manage the exploration-exploitation trade-off. These findings address complementary questions: how effectively the representation models existing data, and how it can guide interactive choices when learning more about a user's interests.
neurips-2024-density-based-user-represen.tldr: GPR4DUR represents user interests as uncertainty-aware densities to support flexible personalized retrieval and exploration.

paragraphs: Multimodal image fusion combines information from different image sources, while object detection identifies objects within the resulting visual information. These tasks are useful for autonomous driving, but coordinating them can require complicated training procedures. E2E-MFD proposes a single-phase, end-to-end training approach that learns fusion and detection together.

Its main mechanism is synchronous joint optimization across components. This is intended to avoid solutions that suit an individual task but are suboptimal for the combined system. The method also coordinates optimization through the gradient matrix of shared parameters. The abstract describes this strategy as ensuring convergence to an optimal fusion-detection configuration.

Evaluations on multiple public datasets report both visually appealing fused images and stronger object detection. Compared with state-of-the-art approaches, the authors report mAP50 increases of 3.9% on M3FD for horizontal detection and 2.0% on DroneVehicle for oriented detection. These results support the practical premise that simplifying training into one coordinated process can accompany improvements in both the visual output and its usefulness for detection.
neurips-2024-e2e-mfd-towards-end-to-end-.tldr: E2E-MFD jointly trains multimodal image fusion and object detection in one phase, improving reported fusion quality and detection performance.

paragraphs: This paper develops CROP to help language models acquire and demonstrate crop-science expertise. It addresses two connected needs: suitable examples for teaching models how to respond in the domain, and a benchmark for measuring their knowledge. Providing both makes it possible to assess whether specialized training actually improves performance on crop-science questions.

The instruction-tuning dataset is assembled through a task-oriented process combining language models and human involvement. It contains 210,038 single-turn dialogues and 1,871 multi-turn dialogues involving crop-science scenarios. The accompanying benchmark contains 5,045 multiple-choice questions organized into three difficulty levels, providing a structured assessment of domain understanding.

Experiments show notable gains on the CROP benchmark after models are fine-tuned using the dataset. That finding supports the usefulness of domain-specific instruction data for the evaluated crop-science tasks. The authors also anticipate wider adoption of language models in crop science and eventual contributions to food production; these are prospective motivations, distinct from the demonstrated improvements in benchmark performance.
neurips-2024-empowering-and-assessing-th.tldr: CROP supplies crop-science instruction data and a knowledge benchmark, with fine-tuning experiments showing improved domain performance.

paragraphs: Iterative hard thresholding is a method for selecting k important entries from a parameter vector in linear regression. It repeatedly updates the parameters during optimization, but computing gradients can dominate its processing time. This paper speeds up that procedure by identifying gradient calculations that can safely be skipped before doing the expensive work.

At each iteration, the method efficiently builds a candidate set containing the important entries. It uses upper bounds on absolute parameter values to exclude entries that do not need to be considered. The central requirement is that pruning must preserve the entries needed by the original method, rather than merely guessing which ones are likely to matter.

Because the pruning is safe, the authors guarantee the same optimization results as ordinary iterative hard thresholding. Their experiments report speedups of up to 73 times without reduced accuracy. The contribution therefore concerns computational efficiency while preserving the underlying optimization outcome: it reduces unnecessary work within the existing procedure instead of trading accuracy for a cheaper approximation.
neurips-2024-fast-iterative-hard-thresho.tldr: Safe pruning skips unnecessary gradient calculations in iterative hard thresholding, preserving its results while achieving experimental speedups of up to 73 times.

paragraphs: Personalizing a text-to-image model from a few reference images can teach it a distinctive style, but controlling individual stylistic attributes through text remains difficult. The problem is especially acute when training uses only a handful of image-text pairs. FineStyle addresses this gap by improving how limited reference material is turned into training examples and how the model is adapted.

Its concept-oriented data scaling creates additional image-text pairs that emphasize different concepts, such as objects, within a style reference image. This gives fine-tuning more concept-focused examples to work with. The method also uses parameter-efficient adapters to tune the key and value kernels in cross-attention layers, concentrating adaptation in components that connect text and visual generation.

The authors evaluate whether generated images follow detailed prompts while remaining faithful to the requested style. Experiments using CLIP scores and human ratings support improvements on these goals. The practical contribution is greater control within personalized generation: users can specify finer details through language while retaining the visual character learned from limited reference material.
neurips-2024-finestyle-fine-grained-cont.tldr: FineStyle expands concept-focused training examples and tunes cross-attention adapters to improve detailed text control over personalized image styles.

paragraphs: Filling missing values in multivariate time series requires recovering several kinds of change across related measurements. The paper distinguishes longer-term trends, seasonal patterns, and residual variation. It finds that residuals are especially important for accurate filling because they capture diverse changes and account for the largest component of imputation error in the authors' analysis.

FGTI responds by bringing frequency information into a generative imputation model. A high-frequency filter strengthens reconstruction of residual variation, while a dominant-frequency filter supports trend and seasonal reconstruction. A cross-domain representation learning module then combines these frequency-based insights with deep representations, so the model can use the complementary information together.

Experiments across datasets containing real-world missing values report improvements in both imputation and downstream applications. The findings support paying explicit attention to residual behavior alongside smoother or recurring patterns. This matters because a filled series can look broadly plausible while still missing the changes that affect later analysis; the proposed design targets that source of error directly.
neurips-2024-frequency-aware-generative-.tldr: FGTI combines frequency filters and deep representations to improve missing-value reconstruction, with particular attention to residual time-series variation.

paragraphs: Deep Transformers can suffer from oversmoothing: representations become increasingly alike across layers until useful distinctions are lost. This can substantially degrade performance even though self-attention is a powerful mechanism for exchanging information. The paper approaches this problem by reconsidering self-attention through graph signal processing.

The authors interpret ordinary self-attention as a simple graph filter and introduce graph-filter-based self-attention, or GFSA. The redesign learns a more general filter, expanding how attention processes information through the graph perspective. Its purpose is to enrich the transformation applied to representations rather than accepting the filtering behavior of the original attention mechanism.

Experiments report improved Transformer performance in computer vision, language processing, graph-level tasks, speech recognition, and code classification. This breadth supports the usefulness of the graph-filter formulation across several application types. The abstract also identifies a concrete cost: GFSA has slightly greater complexity than standard self-attention. The result is an empirical performance improvement accompanied by additional computation, rather than a claim that greater expressiveness is free.
neurips-2024-graph-convolutions-enrich-t.tldr: GFSA redesigns self-attention as a learnable graph filter, improving performance across several domains with slightly higher computational complexity.

paragraphs: Diffusion image generation involves balancing image quality, diversity, and agreement with a prompt or other condition. Classifier-free guidance commonly improves quality and alignment by using an unconditional model to guide a conditional one, but this also reduces variation. The paper investigates whether quality can be controlled without bringing along that diversity cost.

The proposed method guides generation with a smaller, less-trained version of the same model. The authors observe that this weaker companion can improve image quality without compromising the amount of variation. The significant idea is that guidance depends on a relationship between models: a companion need not be a stronger generator to provide useful direction.

Using publicly available networks, the method achieves reported record ImageNet FID scores of 1.01 at 64×64 resolution and 1.25 at 512×512. It also improves unconditional diffusion models, showing that its usefulness extends beyond prompt-conditioned generation. These findings support the possibility of separating quality improvement from reduced diversity through the choice of guidance model.
neurips-2024-guiding-a-diffusion-model-w.tldr: Guiding diffusion generation with a smaller, less-trained version of the model improves reported image quality without reducing variation.

paragraphs: Kernel regression depends on eigenfunctions, which provide a way to describe the functions a kernel can represent. This paper shows through examples that retaining the same collection of eigenfunctions does not guarantee the same regression behavior. Their ordering can substantially affect the outcome, motivating an analysis of how learning responds to that structure.

The authors diagonalize the kernel to obtain a simplified sequence model and introduce an over-parameterized gradient descent method within it. This setup isolates the effects of different orders of a fixed eigenfunction collection. It provides a controlled theoretical setting for examining whether additional parameterization helps learning adapt to the underlying signal.

The theoretical results show that over-parameterized gradient flow can adapt to signal structure and significantly outperform ordinary gradient flow. They also show that deeper over-parameterization can further improve generalization. These are findings about the analyzed sequence-model framework, which the authors use to offer a perspective on why extra parameters may help neural networks beyond what a fixed kernel account captures.
neurips-2024-improving-adaptivity-via-ov.tldr: A sequence-model analysis shows that over-parameterized gradient flow can adapt to signal structure and improve generalization over ordinary gradient flow.

paragraphs: Generating a moving person from text is different from generating a person interacting coherently with a moving object. The latter requires both understanding the requested interaction and modeling how actions affect objects. InterDreamer addresses this task without direct training on paired text and interaction examples, which are difficult to obtain at large scale.

Its central design separates interaction semantics from interaction dynamics. A pretrained language model and a text-to-motion model supply knowledge about what the requested interaction means and the associated human movement. A world model then handles simple physics, modeling how human actions influence object motion. These components provide complementary forms of control over the resulting sequence.

Evaluations on BEHAVE, OMOMO, and CHAIRS demonstrate the framework's ability to produce realistic, coherent 3D interactions aligned with textual directives. The result supports combining pretrained semantic knowledge with a dedicated dynamics model when paired supervision is unavailable. The zero-shot claim specifically concerns text-interaction pairs; the approach still draws on pretrained models and a world model.
neurips-2024-interdreamer-zero-shot-text.tldr: InterDreamer combines pretrained semantic and motion knowledge with a physics-oriented world model to generate 3D interactions without paired text-interaction training.

paragraphs: Before a language model can respond, it must process the prompt during a stage called pre-filling. Attention becomes particularly expensive for very long prompts because its computation grows quadratically with sequence length. MInference targets this bottleneck by computing selected attention interactions efficiently instead of performing the full dense calculation.

The method identifies three recurring structures in long-context attention: A-shape, Vertical-Slash, and Block-Sparse patterns. It chooses a pattern for each attention head offline, then dynamically determines sparse indices during inference. Optimized GPU kernels use those indices to carry out the sparse attention calculations. This combines advance preparation with adaptation to the input being processed.

The approach applies to existing language models without changing pretraining or requiring additional fine-tuning. Evaluations span several long-context models and tasks, including InfiniteBench, RULER, PG-19, and Needle In A Haystack. The authors report up to a tenfold reduction in pre-filling latency on an A100 while maintaining accuracy. That speedup concerns prompt processing specifically, the stage the method is designed to accelerate.
neurips-2024-minference-1-0-accelerating.tldr: MInference uses dynamically selected sparse attention patterns to accelerate long-prompt pre-filling by up to tenfold while maintaining evaluated accuracy.

paragraphs: This paper studies Gaussian kernel regression solutions that interpolate the training data and have minimum norm, without ridge regularization. Its question is how their prediction behavior changes as kernel bandwidth or input dimension varies with sample size. This distinguishes fitting the observed data exactly from generalizing well to new observations.

For fixed input dimension, the authors find that changing or tuning bandwidth does not make the ridgeless solution consistent. With sufficiently large noise, they also find it worse than the null predictor. When dimension grows with sample size, they give a general characterization across dimension-scaling regimes and provide an example of benign overfitting with sub-polynomial dimension growth.

All these results rely on a Gaussian universality ansatz and non-rigorous risk predictions based on kernel eigenstructure. That shared assumption is essential to interpreting the conclusions. Within this analytical framework, the results show a sharp distinction between bandwidth adjustment in fixed dimensions and increasing dimensionality, which can allow successful generalization despite exact fitting of noisy observations.
neurips-2024-overfitting-behaviour-of-ga.tldr: Under stated universality and non-rigorous risk assumptions, the paper characterizes when Gaussian kernel interpolation overfits and when growing dimension permits benign overfitting.

paragraphs: Human feedback does not necessarily reflect a single shared preference: different people may reasonably want different outcomes. Standard reinforcement learning from human feedback can average these differences away, producing inaccurate rewards and poor results for particular groups. This paper develops methods that explicitly represent multiple preference patterns instead of collapsing them into one population-wide target.

The approach infers a user-specific latent variable, an internal representation of preferences, and conditions reward models and policies on it without additional user-specific data. Although the formulation is conceptually simple, the authors find that model architecture and reward scaling require careful handling. The probabilistic representation also supports uncertainty measurement and active learning of preferences.

In simulated control problems, the method infers and optimizes user-specific rewards, helping address tasks whose intended objectives are underspecified. Experiments on language datasets containing diverse preferences show improved reward-model accuracy. Together, these findings support treating disagreement as information about different users, with uncertainty providing an additional way to decide what the system still needs to learn.
neurips-2024-personalizing-reinforcement.tldr: Latent preference modeling personalizes reward models and policies, improving reward accuracy while representing uncertainty about diverse users.

paragraphs: Sequential memory must preserve event order while allowing the same past context to lead to multiple plausible futures. Predictive Attractor Models address this combination through a biologically inspired architecture. PAM learns continuously from a stream, observing each input only once, rather than depending on repeated passes through a sequence.

The model represents past context using lateral inhibition in cortical minicolumns. The authors find that these distinct context representations prevent new memories from overwriting learned knowledge, avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Alongside the predictor, an attractor model learns to generate future outcomes by sampling from a combined set of predicted possibilities, giving the memory a branching generative capability.

Training uses local computations governed by Hebbian plasticity rules, which the authors present as biologically plausible. The paper also discusses noise tolerance, CPU-based learning, and how capacity scales. Its central contribution is a unified approach to retaining sequential knowledge and generating alternative futures, with findings suggesting progress toward computationally efficient memory models inspired by biological learning.
neurips-2024-predictive-attractor-models.tldr: PAM learns sequences in a single online pass, preserves distinct past contexts, and generates multiple possible futures through a companion attractor model.

paragraphs: Optimizing generative models with reinforcement learning often involves PPO, whose stability depends on implementation choices such as value networks and clipping. REBEL seeks a simpler formulation. It turns policy optimization into a regression problem involving the reward difference between two completions of the same prompt, expressed through the policy.

This relative comparison gives the algorithm a lightweight implementation while retaining connections to established reinforcement learning methods. The authors show theoretically that Natural Policy Gradient and other fundamental algorithms can be viewed as REBEL variants, allowing them to match strong existing convergence and sample-complexity guarantees. The framework also accommodates offline data and extensions for intransitive preferences.

Experiments cover language modeling and image generation, reporting performance similar to or stronger than PPO and DPO, with simpler implementation and greater computational efficiency than PPO. Fine-tuning Llama-3-8B-Instruct also produces strong results across the listed language evaluations. The contribution is a common optimization formulation that combines practical simplicity with theoretical links to established policy-learning algorithms.
neurips-2024-rebel-reinforcement-learnin.tldr: REBEL reduces policy optimization to regression on relative rewards, offering theoretical guarantees and competitive generative-model results with a simpler implementation.

paragraphs: Speech separation aims to recover individual voices from a mixture. Many time-domain systems encode audio into learned features and wait until the network's final stage to divide them by speaker. This paper instead separates the feature sequence earlier, adding a speaker dimension so that later processing can work with distinct speaker-specific sequences.

The architecture assigns different jobs to its encoder and decoder. The encoder analyzes the mixture and produces features that are split by speaker. A decoder with shared weights reconstructs the separated sequences while also processing information across speakers. It learns to distinguish speaker features through the separation objective without requiring speaker information.

The authors additionally replace chunk-based dual-path processing with global and local Transformer blocks that directly handle long sequences. Experiments support both the asymmetric architecture and the ability of those blocks to replace processing within and between chunks. The combined model achieves reported state-of-the-art results with substantially less computation across several benchmarks, suggesting that earlier separation and more direct sequence processing work effectively together.
neurips-2024-separate-and-reconstruct-as.tldr: Early speaker-feature separation and global-local Transformer processing improve speech separation while reducing computation in the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: Language models can struggle with complex reasoning and planning, and asking them to revise their own answers does not necessarily solve the problem. AlphaLLM develops a more structured self-improvement loop by combining language models with Monte Carlo Tree Search. The aim is to improve capabilities without requiring additional annotations.

The framework contains three main elements: prompt synthesis, an efficient tree-search approach adapted to language tasks, and three critic models that provide feedback. These components address the need for training material, the large space of possible language continuations, and the difficulty of evaluating responses. Search and criticism give the loop a way to explore and assess candidate reasoning paths.

Experiments on mathematical reasoning show significant performance improvements without additional annotations. This supports the potential of combining generated prompts, structured exploration, and learned feedback for self-improvement. The demonstrated result concerns mathematical reasoning; the wider motivation includes complex planning, but the abstract's experimental evidence is specifically tied to the mathematical tasks evaluated.
neurips-2024-toward-self-improvement-of-.tldr: AlphaLLM combines prompt synthesis, tree search, and critic models to improve mathematical reasoning without additional annotations.

paragraphs: Most vision-language models use a separate vision encoder to convert images into features for a language model. That encoder introduces assumptions about visual representation, including resolution, aspect ratio, and semantic content. This paper explores removing it, while addressing the slow convergence and performance gaps observed when encoder-free models are trained directly.

The proposed training recipe has two central elements: connecting visual and language representations within a unified decoder, and adding supervision that strengthens visual recognition. Together, these strategies produce EVE, an encoder-free vision-language model designed for efficient training and inference. The contribution is therefore both an architecture direction and a practical recipe for making it work.

Trained using 35 million publicly accessible data examples, EVE rivals encoder-based models of similar capacity across multiple vision-language benchmarks. It also substantially outperforms Fuyu-8B in the reported comparison. These findings show that a separate vision encoder is not required to achieve competitive results in these evaluations, and support a more transparent route toward unified decoder-based processing across modalities.
neurips-2024-unveiling-encoder-free-visi.tldr: EVE uses unified-decoder training and extra visual supervision to make encoder-free vision-language modeling competitive with similarly sized encoder-based models.
